# Draft:Paris Dawarzarei

----
= Paris Dawarzarei =
Paris Dawarzarei is a young and upcoming composer. In addition to composing, he holds a high level within Trumpet/Bb and Soprano Cornet playing.
As a composer, Dawarzarei stands out for his emotional clarity and strong architectural sense. His works are often dramatic and intense, but never empty. Every section has purpose. He uses harmony boldly, builds tension patiently, and releases it with impact. His music speaks directly, without hiding behind effects or gimmicks.
History
Paris Dawarzarei has a background that moves across school bands, jazz ensembles, and brass band tradition.
He started in Norwegian school band (skolekorps) culture, including Toridal Skolemusikkorps, where he developed his early foundation in brass playing, ensemble discipline, and reading within structured band settings.
Alongside this, he became active in jazz and big band environments. He has played in Sørnorsk Ungdomsstorband, where he worked with larger jazz ensemble repertoire, and sectional playing in a more flexible stylistic context.
He has also worked in smaller jazz groups such as The Paris Jazz Quartet, exploring more intimate ensemble playing and improvisation based formats. In addition, he has appeared as a guest musician with ensembles such as Red Note Quartet, contributing in a featured role within a small ensemble jazz setting.
Today, he plays in Molde Brass Band, where he is active in the brass band scene. His playing there sits within the competitive and concert oriented brass band tradition, while still reflecting his broader background in jazz and big band environments.
The [https://brassfestival.no/ Oslo Brass Festival] is a two day brass band competition in Oslo where bands from 3rd division up to the Elite division take part in two different performances: one church concert and one concert at Sentrum Scene, each with its own programme.
Paris Dawarzarei served as the "live-adjudicator" at the 2026 festival and adjudicated all bands across every division (3rd to Elite division), hearing both their church concert and their Sentrum Scene performance over the two days.
Landslinja for jazz interprets Sun Ra Arkestra
The “Landslinja for jazz interprets Sun Ra Arkestra” concert at the Molde International Jazz Festival was a large ensemble performance built around Sun Ra’s music and performance concept.
Rather than being fully written out in advance, the project was developed through rehearsal as a collective interpretation. According to the festival’s own description, the process was built around Sun Ra material in a way where “anything can happen”, focusing on ensemble interaction and improvisation rather than strict reconstruction of arrangements.
A press summary of the project also describes it as a collaborative process between students and musicians, where the performance was shaped through rehearsal and then completed in real time on stage.
Musically, the concert moved between structured ensemble sections and freer, open passages. The sound was driven by full ensemble energy, shifting dynamics, and improvisation that moved in and out of collective form rather than just highlighting individual solos.
Paris Dawarzarei performed in the trumpet section of this ensemble. His role was part of the larger group sound, contributing to the brass texture and overall ensemble direction rather than fixed written lines.
In summary, the concert was a live, evolving interpretation of Sun Ra’s music, built from rehearsed material, but ultimately shaped on stage through improvisation and ensemble decision-making.
Key facts
Profession: Composer, Jazz musician and Brass musician
Primary instruments: Trumpet, cornet, soprano cornet
Active since: Early 2020s
Performance regions: Norway, Northern Europe
Notable musical works/releases:
Dawar No. 3 – Duet for Trumpet and Piano (Live Performance) (2023).
"Ode to" Karl Neipl and Peter Ewinger - For Soprano Cornet and Eb Tuba. (Commissioned by Arkivet (Kristiansand))
Blood to Marble (Musical work for bass band - Youth Band)
A 27 V.6.7 (Musical work for Molde Brass Band)
Completos - Adagio I (Musical work for Agder Symfoniorkester)
Paris Dawarzarei has been awarded the TEFT stipend, a support grant given to young musicians working within the Norwegian music scene.
The stipend recognises emerging artists for their artistic development and contribution to their field, often supporting further work in performance, composition, or project development.
